summary: Indonesia's fire record comes from heat-sensing satellites (MODIS, VIIRS), and smoke, cloud and smouldering peat can hide fires from them. BlindSpot uses NASA-ISRO NISAR L-band radar, which sees through smoke, to map land change across a 50 x 50 km peat landscape near Sampit, Central Kalimantan, over the 2026 fire season, and checks every change patch against NASA FIRMS hotspots. Result: 71% of radar-detected change had no fire hotspot recorded (range 61 to 75%), most of it early in the season: 82% from late August to September, 23% in October. An interactive web app shows every patch, its radar history and the evidence, with honest uncertainty. A place to look, every 12 days.
details: HOW IT WORKS. (1) We stream the study window of 11 NISAR L2 GCOV images (18 Jun to 28 Oct 2026, track 061, frame 090, HH and HV) onto a 60 m grid. (2) Each date is normalised by its scene-wide ratio to the June to July reference, which cancels rain, soil moisture and calibration shifts. (3) A sequential omnibus test (Conradsen et al. 2016; Canty et al. 2020) at a 1% false-alarm rate, with effective looks measured from the reference dates, finds the first date each pixel changed; HV must stay at least 1 dB down for two dates, and patches of 1 ha or more are kept. Pixels already drying within the reference, water and the radar's swath edge are handled explicitly. (4) A patch counts as "recorded" if a NASA FIRMS VIIRS or MODIS hotspot lies within 1 km of it between the previous radar date and the change date. (5) The headline is the area share of change with no hotspot recorded, with a 300-run Monte Carlo range (hotspot position, 0.5 to 2 km buffer, 0 to 12 days slack). VALIDATION. Synthetic burns injected into the real radar: about 3 ha and up detected every time at drops of 4 dB or more; false alarms on 0.006% of stable land. A 48-point labelled stratified sample gives an Olofsson (2014) error-adjusted area of 221 km² (95% CI 0 to 496 km²). 10 patches reviewed by hand: 3 fire supported, 6 other disturbance, 1 unresolved. RADD radar alerts overlap 0.2% of patches. The 17 Aug pass, the first after a 24-day acquisition gap, is reported separately: without it the share is 59%. KEY FEATURES. Interactive map with an 11-date timeline, before and after views, per-patch radar history and evidence, a "Why radar" explainer with real NASA imagery of the smoke over our study area, and a Method page with every formula and a table of uncertainty sources. BENEFITS AND IMPACT. A screening tool for analysts, journalists and peat agencies: it shows where land changed under the smoke and what the hotspot record says, especially early in the fire season, when the record missed most. It never claims who caused a change or that a patch is a missed fire: "no hotspot recorded" is a place to look. NISAR revisits almost all of Earth's land every 12 days, and the pipeline is built to run on any track. CREATIVITY. Instead of another change viewer, BlindSpot uses radar to audit the fire record itself, with an honest uncertainty range on every number. TOOLS. Python (numpy, xarray, rasterio, geopandas, shapely, scipy), earthaccess and h5py for streaming NISAR; a statistical test with no machine learning; a static web app (Leaflet, Chart.js, KaTeX, WebGL globe) on GitHub Pages; GitHub Actions to package outputs and deploy. Code: https://github.com/abd2467/blindspot REFERENCES. Conradsen et al. (2016) IEEE TGRS; Canty, Nielsen, Conradsen and Skriver (2020) Remote Sensing; Olofsson et al. (2014) Remote Sensing of Environment; Sofiev and Kouznetsov (2026) Geoscientific Model Development; NASA Earth Observatory (Sep 2026); NEA haze updates (Sep to Oct 2026). AI USE. The idea, research direction, method choices, design and construction of BlindSpot are the team's original work. Claude (Anthropic) was used as a tool to help with coding, data checks and wording; every result comes from the pipeline outputs in the repository. CodeRabbit reviewed every pull request, and a Floorplan map of the codebase (an interactive architecture diagram made with Claude) was used to plan and check how the pipeline stages connect.
